name: Museum of Modern Art
notes:
Address/hours confirmed via moma.org. Large multi-exhibition institution — at add time the site lists 'Marcel Duchamp' (through Aug 22), 'Frida and Diego: The Last Dream' (through Sep 12), 'Pierre Huyghe: UUmwelt' (through Nov 29), and 'Architects of Liberation: Modernism in Western Africa' (through 2027-01-02) as concurrently on view; not individually entered as manual records here, left for a proper crawl/adapter pass.

Fingerprint (2026-08-19): sanity — cdn.sanity.io/images/476nwnl9/production/ references in page markup (project id 476nwnl9); dataset 'production' is public and queryable with no auth. INVESTIGATED 2026-08-19 to wire the live adapter and found it's a dead end: the '_type == "exhibition"' document type has exactly 2 documents, both obvious placeholder/test content ('The best exhibition', 'Film Exhibition Test'), not real MoMA shows. A second type, 'galleryExhibition' (204 documents, permanent-collection floor-rotation labels like 'Gallery 505', not the headline special exhibitions), has real content but every single document fails even this adapter's lenient recency filter (closes today-or-later, or opened within the last 120 days) — zero pass. So whichever type gets wired up, the live query returns nothing useful; wiring it would add config complexity for the same empty result staying on manual already gives, with the added risk of plausible()-gating churn if it ever flips between 0 and a stray result. MoMA's real headline-exhibition content isn't reachable through this public Sanity project at all — evidently served some other way (a different backend/project, or server-rendered from an internal API). Staying on manual; this isn't the 'easy win' it looked like from the CDN fingerprint alone.
